title: “You Can See Everything” and the nature of liars
gist: Noah Smith reviews Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes documentary and uses it to argue Holmes is a continuous, automatic liar; the text is truncated by a paywall before the Type 1 versus Type 2 liar framework.

themes.theme: Elizabeth Holmes and the psychology of lying

insights.claim: Elizabeth Holmes is a documented deliberate fraudster: she showed investors fake financial results in 2015, added fake pharmaceutical logos to Theranos reports, and admitted in court concealing that Theranos diluted blood samples.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Fraud red flags at private startups often include fabricated reports; diligence should verify independently.

insights.claim: Smith argues the Nathan Fielder film You Can See Everything works by capturing moments that reveal Holmes's relationship to truth, such as repeatedly asserting obviously false claims with a sincere expression, rather than catching a single lie.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Pathological, continuous deception is a different risk from occasional lying when evaluating founders.

insights.claim: Smith claims Holmes is a special kind of liar for whom deception and manipulation are as automatic and continuous as breathing, and previews a Type 1 versus Type 2 liar distinction (the rest is paywalled).
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Distinguishing habitual from situational liars is a founder-evaluation heuristic.
insights.quote: someone for whom deception and manipulation are as automatic and as continuous as breathing
